title: Has King David's Palace in Jerusalem Been Found?
author: Israel Finkelstein; Ze'ev Herzog; Lily Singer-Avitz; David Ussishkin
publisher: Tel Aviv (journal of the Institute of Archaeology, Tel Aviv University), vol. 34, no. 2
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted peer-reviewed journal article. Project stores its own summary of the argument only; no reproduction of the article's text, plans, or photographs.
summary: The direct, named scholarly rebuttal of Eilat Mazar's 'Large Stone Structure = David's palace' identification (see mazar-2009-palace-of-david). The authors argue that the exposed walls are poorly preserved and not demonstrably part of one coherent building; that the pottery Mazar used to date the complex to the 10th century BCE does not securely do so and is compatible with a later Iron Age date; and, more pointedly, that the excavation and its publicized interpretation were shaped by a prior commitment to the biblical narrative rather than by the archaeological evidence read independently of it. This project cites this article as the named, checkable minimalist/critical counter-view to Mazar's identification, not as a settled redating.
